results.quote: If the parameter \(\alpha\) satisfies the condition \(\alpha>\frac{b-c}{2}\), where \(c=x^*Tx>0,b=x^*WT^{-1}Wx\ge 0\), with \(x\in\mathbb{C}^n\) such that \(\|x\|_2=1\), then the iterative scheme defined in (9) converges to the unique solution for any initial guess \(x^{(0)}\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

Under the assumptions of Theorem 1, the eigenvalues of the preconditioned matrix \(\mathscr{P}_{\text{\textit{VBP}}}^{-1}\mathscr{A}\) are real and positive, and lie in the interval \(\sigma(\mathscr{P}_{\text{\textit{VBP}}}^{-1}\mathscr{A})\subset\left[\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(T)+\sigma_{\mathrm{min}}^2(W)/\lambda_{\mathrm{max}}(T)}{\alpha+\lambda_{\mathrm{max}}(T)},\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{max}}(T)+\sigma_{\mathrm{max}}^2(W)/\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(T)}{\alpha+\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(T)}\right]\).

results.bound: \text{GMRES terminates in at most }n+1\text{ steps (minimal polynomial degree }\le n+1\text{)}
results.quote: Theorem 5 shows that with the VBP preconditioner \(\mathscr{P}_{\mathrm{VBP}}\), termination (in exact arithmetic) of the GMRES method will occur in at most \(n+1\) steps for any choice of the right hand side \(\mathbf{d}\).
